table.title: Anglo-Chinese Calendar, 1926
table.context: A printed Anglo-Chinese calendar for 1926 aligning Western dates, weekdays and Chinese lunar days by month, with lunar month markers printed within the lunar rows.
transcriber_notes: Transcribed by Claude Haiku 5.5 (via API) from page crops, one reading; not checked by eye.

table.title: [Anglo-Chinese Calendar for 1926 — July to December, Chinese Moon Days, Gregorian Dates and Weekdays]
footnotes: Chinese moon-month names (VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, XI) are printed beside the first day of each new moon and are not transcribed as cells.
The printed columns carry no day headings; slots run from left to right across each month band, with a dash (—) printed where the calendar is blank.
table.context: This Anglo-Chinese calendar shows, for each Gregorian month of July to December 1926, the matching Chinese moon day, date and weekday, so readers can convert between the two systems.
transcriber_notes: Transcribed by Claude Haiku 5.5 (via API) from page crops, one reading; not checked by eye.

table.title: Anglo-Chinese Calendar, 1927 (January to June)
footnotes: Chinese moon-month markers (XII, N.Y., II, III, IV, V, VI) are printed beside the first day of each Chinese month and are not transcribed as separate cells.
table.context: This Anglo-Chinese calendar for January to June 1927 pairs Chinese lunar dates with Gregorian dates and weekdays, so readers can convert between the two systems.

table.title: [Opium and Drugs Seized and Burned in Peking, March 1925]
footnotes: Morphia mixture for pill making: varying from a few ounces to flour sacks.
